This Month

The theme of the month

Peach Season

August is Peach Season. Peak summer, peak heat and the best fruit of the year. This month is built on bright, high-protein plates that come together fast, so a hot kitchen, a busy week or a weekend away never knocks you off track.

This month's focus

Protein first, always, with the fruit August does best. Peaches, berries and melon alongside grilled protein, crisp salads and cold bowls. Light on the stomach, high in protein.

What to expect

Fast, no-fuss summer food. Plenty of no-cook lunches, cold bowls and high-protein sweets, simple enough for the hottest week of the year when you would rather be outside.

How these meals support your goal

Every plate is high in protein and easy to repeat. Keep protein high, lean on your favourites and stay consistent, and your Peach Season shape takes care of itself.

Peach Season · 7-Day Meal Mini Challenge

One small food habit a day for seven days, the meal-plan twin of your Peach Season training challenge. Tick them off as you go.

Day 1
Plan your week and write your shopping list
Day 2
Protein first at every main meal
Day 3
Prep one breakfast or snack ahead
Day 4
Hit 2 litres of water before dinner
Day 5
Build one no-cook plate on a hot day
Day 6
Make one high-protein sweet
Day 7
Pick three repeat meals for next week

Your Plan

How to follow your meal plan

Same 28 recipes for everyone. Your goal sets your portions, your protein target and how much extra fuel you add.

Fat Loss Foundation
Lean, light + consistent
Base portions
Calories
Approx. 1,500–1,700 kcal per day.
Protein
Approx. 100–130g protein per day.
How to follow the meals
Use the recipes as written, keep portions moderate and repeat the meals that feel easiest.
If you need less food
Reduce carb or fat portions slightly before cutting protein.
Balanced Toning
Fuel training + stay lean
Standard plan
Calories
Approx. 1,700–1,900 kcal per day.
Protein
Approx. 110–140g protein per day.
How to follow the meals
Use one breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack each day, then adjust around hunger and activity.
If you need more fuel
Add a snack, extra fruit or a slightly bigger carb portion around training.
Glute Growth
Build shape + support recovery
Higher-fuel option
Calories
Approx. 1,900–2,200 kcal per day.
Protein
Approx. 120–160g protein per day.
How to follow the meals
Keep protein high and increase carbs around training so your glutes have enough fuel to grow.
If progress stalls
Check food, sleep and training consistency before adding more volume or cutting meals.
Simple rules
  • Prioritise protein at every meal.
  • Build meals around foods you enjoy.
  • Add vegetables freely.
  • Stay hydrated.
  • Repeat meals if it makes life easier.
Low-oil cooking

Use low-oil cooking methods where possible: air fryer, oven, grill, non-stick pan, water sautéing, lemon, spices and low-cal sauces.

Small changes like these keep meals light without losing any flavour.

🍒

Calories are a guide, not a personalised prescription. Protein, consistency and portion awareness are the priority.

Macros are estimates and may vary depending on brands, portion sizes and swaps. Use them as a guide.

🍒The Model Body ClubPeach Season
Make It Yours

Adapt & swap

Do not like an ingredient, or got something else in? Swap it. Keep the protein anchor, trade like for like, and the meal still works.

🍒
The golden rule

Keep the protein anchor, then swap like for like. If a swap lowers protein, add another protein source or increase the portion.

Animal protein

100g chicken → 100g lean turkey / 120g prawns / 120g white fish / 120g salmon. Adjust fats where needed.

Plant protein

180–200g tofu → 120–140g tempeh / seitan
or 150–200g edamame / lentils / chickpeas.

Eggs

2 eggs → egg whites / tofu scramble / extra protein powder depending on recipe.

Dairy-free

Milk → almond, oat or soya. Yoghurt → dairy-free high-protein yoghurt. Butter → dairy-free spread, olive, avocado or coconut oil.

Carbs

Rice, pasta, potatoes, wraps, bread, oats, noodles and quinoa. Swap like for like.

Fats

Avocado, nuts, nut butter, seeds, olive oil and salmon. Keep portions moderate.

Veg & flavour

Swap veg one for one, fresh or frozen. Herbs, spices, lemon, lime, vinegar, mustard and low-cal sauces add flavour.

Sweet snacks

Fruit, protein yoghurt, protein bars, dark chocolate, rice cakes, dates, frozen grapes or homemade high-protein sweets.

🍒

Swaps are flexible. Keep the meal balanced, keep protein high, and choose what you actually enjoy.

Sourdough, Soft-Boiled Eggs & Green Goddess Salad
Jammy eggs, crisp salad and a creamy herb dressing.
Serves
1
Prep
10 min
Cook
8 min

485kcal
Protein

Macros are estimates and may vary depending on brands, portion sizes and swaps. Use them as a guide. Use cooked or uncooked weights exactly as written in each recipe.
💪
High protein
24g per serving
High ProteinDairy FreeOil Free20 Min
Why you'll love it

A brunch-style plate that lands protein, greens and good carbs in one go.

Ingredients
  • 2 slices sourdough bread (80g)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 30g baby spinach
  • 75g cucumber, diced
  • 50g avocado, diced
  • Fresh chives, chopped
  • Green Goddess Dressing
  • 40g dairy-free Greek-style yoghurt
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • 1 tsp Dijon mustard
  • 1 tbsp fresh parsley
  • 1 tbsp fresh chives
  • 1 small garlic clove
  • Salt & black pepper
  • Splash of water to loosen
Method
  1. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil and cook the eggs for 7–8 minutes. Transfer to iced water before peeling.
  2. Toast the sourdough until golden.
  3. Blend the yoghurt, lemon juice, Dijon, parsley, chives, garlic, seasoning and a splash of water until smooth.
  4. Toss the spinach, cucumber and avocado with the dressing.
  5. Serve alongside the toasted sourdough and soft-boiled eggs.
Tips & notes

Iced water stops the eggs cooking and keeps the yolks jammy. Make the dressing ahead and keep it in a jar for the week.

High protein
43g per serving
High ProteinDairy FreeOil Free15 Min
Why you'll love it

43g of protein in a bowl of oats, without a chalky protein-powder finish.

Ingredients
  • 50g oats
  • 20g vanilla protein powder
  • 1 whole egg
  • 100g egg whites
  • 180ml unsweetened almond milk
  • ½ tsp vanilla extract
  • ½ tsp cinnamon
  • Pinch of salt
  • 80g fresh strawberries, diced
  • Protein Cream
  • 100g dairy-free Greek-style yoghurt
  • 10g vanilla protein powder
  • To Finish
  • Fresh strawberries, sliced
Method
  1. Add the oats, almond milk, vanilla, cinnamon and salt to a saucepan over a medium heat.
  2. Cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the oats begin to thicken.
  3. Reduce the heat to low.
  4. Whisk the egg and egg whites together, then pour slowly into the oats while stirring continuously until smooth and creamy.
  5. Stir through the vanilla protein powder and diced strawberries.
  6. Spoon into a bowl.
  7. Mix the yoghurt and protein powder until smooth, then spoon over the oats.
  8. Finish with sliced fresh strawberries.
Tips & notes

Stirring the egg in continuously over a low heat is what makes these creamy rather than scrambled. Do not rush it.

High ProteinLow CarbDairy FreeOil Free
Why you'll love it

35g of protein for 360 calories, and it still eats like a proper brunch.

Ingredients
  • Omelette
  • 200g egg whites
  • 1 whole egg
  • 60g spinach
  • 2 spring onions, sliced
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • Salt & black pepper
  • Avocado Salsa
  • ½ avocado, diced
  • 100g cherry tomatoes, diced
  • ¼ small red onion, finely diced
  • Juice of ½ lime
  • Fresh coriander, chopped
  • 1 small jalapeño, finely diced (optional)
  • Salt & black pepper
  • To Serve
  • Handful of rocket
  • Extra coriander
  • Lime wedges
Method
  1. Combine all the avocado salsa ingredients in a bowl and set aside.
  2. Whisk the egg whites, whole egg, garlic powder, salt and pepper together.
  3. Pour into a hot non-stick pan and scatter over the spinach and spring onions.
  4. Cook over a low-medium heat until just set, then fold the omelette in half.
  5. Transfer to a plate and spoon the avocado salsa generously over the top.
  6. Finish with fresh coriander, rocket and a squeeze of lime.
Tips & notes

Make the salsa just before serving. The lime keeps the avocado from browning and adds the zesty finish.

High ProteinDairy FreeOil FreeMeal Prep
Why you'll love it

Zero effort in the morning and it genuinely tastes like peach cobbler.

Ingredients
  • ½ cup oats
  • 1 scoop vanilla protein powder
  • 1 tbsp chia seeds
  • ¾ cup unsweetened almond or soy milk
  • ⅓ cup dairy-free high-protein yoghurt
  • 1 small peach, diced
  • ½ tsp cinnamon
  • ½ tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 tsp maple syrup (optional)
  • Topping
  • Extra diced peach
  • Sprinkle of cinnamon
  • 1 tbsp crushed granola
Method
  1. Add the oats, protein powder, chia seeds, milk, yoghurt, cinnamon, vanilla and maple syrup to a jar or bowl.
  2. Stir well until smooth.
  3. Fold through half the diced peach.
  4. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
  5. Top with the remaining peach, cinnamon and granola before serving.
Tips & notes

The chia seeds thicken it while you sleep, so it is properly spoonable by morning.

💪
High protein
21g per serving
High ProteinDairy FreeOil FreeMeal Prep
Why you'll love it

Make them once, eat them all week. The grated courgette keeps them moist without adding much at all.

Ingredients
  • 8 whole eggs
  • 1 cup (250ml) egg whites
  • 1 small courgette, grated and squeezed dry
  • 1 red pepper, finely diced
  • 1 cup spinach, chopped
  • ½ red onion, finely diced
  • ½ cup cooked lean chicken or turkey, diced (optional)
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • Black pepper
  • Fresh chives or parsley (optional)
Method
  1. Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
  2. Grate the courgette and squeeze out as much liquid as possible using a clean tea towel or kitchen paper.
  3. Divide the courgette, pepper, spinach, onion and chicken, if using, between a 12-hole muffin tin lined with silicone cases.
  4. Whisk together the eggs, egg whites, garlic powder, paprika and black pepper.
  5. Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables until each cup is about three quarters full.
  6. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until puffed up and fully set.
  7. Leave to cool for 5 minutes before removing from the tin.
Tips & notes

Makes 12 muffins, roughly 60 kcal and 7g protein each. Keeps in the fridge for 4 days or the freezer for 2 months. Reheat for 30–60 seconds.

High protein

High ProteinDairy FreeOil FreeWeekend
Why you'll love it

Sweet burst tomatoes against smoky chilli kale, with jammy eggs to pull it together.

Ingredients
  • Roasted Tomatoes
  • 150g cherry tomatoes
  • 1 tsp balsamic vinegar
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • Salt & black pepper
  • Spicy Kale
  • 60g kale
  • ½ tsp smoked paprika
  • ½ tsp chilli flakes, to taste
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • To Serve
  • 2 slices sourdough, toasted
  • 2 soft-boiled eggs
  • Fresh chives, chopped
  • Cracked black pepper
Method
  1. Roast the cherry tomatoes at 200°C for 18–20 minutes with the balsamic vinegar, garlic powder, salt and pepper until soft and bursting.
  2. Add the kale to a non-stick pan with a splash of water. Stir in the smoked paprika, chilli flakes and garlic powder and cook for 3–4 minutes until tender. Finish with a squeeze of lemon.
  3. Soft-boil the eggs for 7 minutes, then peel and halve.
  4. Toast the sourdough.
  5. Plate the sourdough with the spicy kale, roasted tomatoes and soft-boiled eggs. Finish with fresh chives and cracked black pepper.
Tips & notes

Roast the tomatoes until they actually burst. That is where the sweetness comes from to balance the smoky kale.

High ProteinDairy FreeOil FreeWeekend
Why you'll love it

A slow Sunday stack that still lands 42g of protein.

Ingredients
  • Pancakes
  • 50g oat flour
  • 20g vanilla protein powder
  • 1 whole egg
  • 100g egg whites
  • 80ml plant milk of choice
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • 80g fresh blueberries
  • To Serve
  • 100g dairy-free Greek-style yoghurt
  • Extra blueberries
  • Lemon zest
  • 1 tsp maple syrup or honey (optional)
Method
  1. Whisk the oat flour, protein powder and baking powder together in a bowl.
  2. Add the egg, egg whites, plant milk and lemon zest and whisk until smooth.
  3. Gently fold through the blueberries.
  4. Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat.
  5. Spoon the batter into the pan to make 3–4 pancakes and cook for 2–3 minutes on each side until golden and cooked through.
  6. Stack and top with the dairy-free yoghurt, extra blueberries, lemon zest and a drizzle of maple syrup or honey if you like.
Tips & notes

Fold the blueberries in at the very end so they stay whole and burst as the pancakes cook.

High ProteinDairy FreeOil Free10 Min
Why you'll love it

Sushi-shop flavour in ten minutes, no cooking and no washing up.

Ingredients
  • Spicy Tuna
  • 1 x 145g tin tuna in spring water, drained
  • 2 tbsp dairy-free Greek-style yoghurt
  • 1 tsp sriracha
  • 1 tsp sweet chilli sauce
  • 1 tsp reduced-salt soy sauce
  • 1 tsp lime juice
  • Wraps
  • 6 roasted seaweed snack sheets, or 3 full nori sheets cut in half
  • ½ avocado, sliced
  • ¼ cucumber, cut into matchsticks
  • 1 small carrot, cut into matchsticks
  • 2 spring onions, sliced
  • Sesame seeds
  • Pickled ginger (optional)
Method
  1. Mix the tuna with the yoghurt, sriracha, sweet chilli, soy sauce and lime juice.
  2. Lay out the nori sheets.
  3. Top each with the spicy tuna mixture.
  4. Add the avocado, cucumber, carrot and spring onions.
  5. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
  6. Fold and enjoy immediately.
Tips & notes

Keep the veg very thinly sliced and only assemble just before eating so the nori stays crisp.

  5. Finish with the remaining blueberries, biscuit crumbs or granola, and lemon zest.
  6. Chill before serving if you prefer it cold.
Tips & notes

Add the biscuit crumbs just before eating so they stay crunchy.

Dairy FreeOil FreeBatchSweet
Why you'll love it

Make once, slice into eight, and the sweet fix is sorted for the week.

Ingredients
  • 1 cup oat flour
  • ½ cup vanilla protein powder
  • ⅓ cup almond butter or cashew butter
  • ¼ cup maple syrup
  • 2 tbsp unsweetened shredded coconut
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • 2–3 tbsp almond milk
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • Optional topping
  • Extra coconut
  • Drizzle of melted dairy-free white chocolate
Method
  1. Mix the oat flour, protein powder, coconut and lemon zest in a bowl.
  2. Add the almond butter, maple syrup, lemon juice and almond milk.
  3. Stir until a soft dough forms.
  4. Press into a lined small container or loaf tin.
  5. Chill for 1–2 hours, until firm.
  6. Slice into 8 squares.
Tips & notes

Macros are per square. Keep them in the fridge so they hold their shape.

High ProteinDairy FreeOil FreeBatch
Why you'll love it

A grab-and-go sweet fix that actually carries protein.

Ingredients
  • Makes 8 balls
  • 100g oat flour
  • 30g vanilla protein powder
  • 2 tbsp almond butter
  • 2 tbsp maple syrup or honey
  • 2–3 tbsp plant milk of choice
  • 20g dark chocolate chips
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
Method
  1. Add the oat flour, protein powder and chocolate chips to a bowl.
  2. Stir in the almond butter, maple syrup or honey and vanilla extract.
  3. Add the plant milk a little at a time until a soft cookie dough forms.
  4. Roll into 8 equal balls.
  5. Chill in the fridge for 20–30 minutes before serving.
Tips & notes

Macros are per serving of 2 balls. Keep a batch in the fridge, they taste better chilled.

High ProteinDairy FreeOil Free5 Min
Why you'll love it

28g of protein in a jar that eats like a proper dessert.

Ingredients
  • Protein Pudding
  • 150g dairy-free Greek-style yoghurt
  • 20g vanilla protein powder
  • 2–3 tbsp plant milk of choice, if needed to loosen
  • Layers
  • ½ banana, sliced
  • 1 crushed oat biscuit or 1 crushed Weetabix
  • Sprinkle of cinnamon
Method
  1. Mix the dairy-free yoghurt and vanilla protein powder until smooth. Add a splash of plant milk for a creamier consistency.
  2. In a small glass or jar, layer half the protein pudding, half the banana slices and half the crushed biscuit.
  3. Repeat the layers.
  4. Finish with a sprinkle of cinnamon.
  5. Chill for 20–30 minutes before serving for the best texture.
Tips & notes

Chilling lets the biscuit layer soften into that classic banana pudding texture. Worth the wait.

Your Club

Keep going

August will not be a perfect month and it does not need to be. Keep protein high, lean on the meals you like and let the rest flex. Here is how to make Peach Season count, and roll it into the next.

🍒
Repeat your favourites
The meals you come back to are the ones that get results. Pick three from this month and repeat them.
🍒
Pair with Peach Season training
The Peach Season training plan is the twin of this one, same theme, same challenge. Pair the two, or let the meals stand on their own.
🍒
Share your wins
Tag @KassyAlicee. Your progress might be someone else's start.
🍒
Come back next month
A fresh drop lands every month, new meals, new theme, same simple approach.

August is the month most people let slide. Heat, holidays, plans every weekend. You do not need a perfect month, you need three meals you can repeat with your eyes shut. Build Peach Season around those and September looks after itself.
